title: The far future: heat death and proton decay
example_questions: What happens in a trillion trillion years?
summary: With a cosmological constant, the universe expands forever. Stars stop forming, the last stars burn out, black holes evaporate by Hawking radiation, and the universe approaches a cold, dark, nearly empty heat death. If protons decay, as many grand unified theories predict, even ordinary matter eventually dissolves, though experiments show protons live far longer than the current age of the universe.
support_note: The standard expectation for a universe with a cosmological constant; proton decay is unconfirmed.
what_happens: Star formation ends and the last stars fade
Dead stars and black holes dominate
A cold, dilute, dark universe remains
